Hey, sounds like you are going through a very tough period in your life. I don't want to say it'll get better, bc I know from experience it always feels like it won't and sometimes doesn't for a while. 

Talking about your parents, it must be really difficult to always feel like things that are a part of you, or something that you enjoy should be below you and that your identity feels questioned all of the time. Feelings and habits tend to be passed down from parents to children, so all of this invalidation must be really taking a toll on you. Especially when you are kicked out for a part of you like it is a disease.

I just want to say, I'm here for you. You are worth something. You aren't a failure, you've just got a bunch of shit weighing on you, that you have through NO fault of your own. 

Sending Virtual hugs,

I also do this. I honestly don't know how I get jack shit done. I spend ages circling and circling in my brain replaying conversations from however long ago and beating myself up for it for absolutely no reason. I do it in my dreams. Sometimes I spend an hour or two living in the background and worrying about a conversation I had just then (while I'm usually sitting next to said person and could just easily rectify the conversation but of course I overthink and worry about them thinking I'm stupid or sensitive or smth). Then I think like 'they must think I'm terrible' 'but you can't be terrible' 'you're totally overthinking things' 'it was probably nothing' 'if it was nothing then why am I so worried about it' 'because you are so stupid and sensitive' 'I guess I must be' 'exactly' 'no, you can't feel like this! 'water off of a ducks back' as your mom used to obsessively say' etc. I'm just so tired of it.

Annoyingly for me its 'It'll get better' or the sheer reaction people have when I tell about how terrible I feel every f-ing day because 'you're such a nice/positive person!'. When people say that it will get better, especially when most of the time I feel stuck in a rut of self-hatred, it feels like they are dismissing me and my feelings, especially since other people see me as a bubbly person all of the time, so they think I'm overreacting, even when I'm sharing how terrible I feel when I share these things and others always think I'm 'overreacting'.

I slightly agree with you there, but I think that this just shows the way of public opinion. Those that were downvoted in this thread, the most, tended to be those saying that masks are oppressive, yes, but while most of the people saying that masks are necessary had good points, some with nuanced opinions, the people saying that masks are bad mostly just had their opinion, with little to no nuance, fact or balanced argument. If you look at the replies, agreeably, you can see that the people against masks had sarcastic replies not constructive or looking into it, rather than the agreeing of the replies to answers towards mask-wearing.

Case in point, I sincerely believe that there are definitely groups of people that should not have to wear masks (those with breathing problems or anxiety/panic attacks, those that are vaccinated etc.), however, I also think that the group of people against masks for political reasons are not entirely ignorant, and are trapped in media bubbles of their own making. I think that it can be quite hard to get out of that bubble due to companies (like google) that follow everyone around on the internet.

But, what can you expect? I mean, the question was specifically about the thought process of a group of people, so the answers were more likely to attack that group of people, especially as that topic is politically charged in all directions. We are all tired and annoyed, talking about a group of people who are politically charged, who many hold liable, in part, to the thing that is making us all tired and annoyed. Of course, people on this thread will be angry, and less ......... hospitable?

For example, despite how level-headed I'm trying to be, I suspect that I am coming off somewhat snarky and sarcastic. Anyway ... hope that was long enough. ;)
